revisions.title: Clean the main circulating heater back to its clean performance

changes.physical_change: Clean E-201 circulating heater tubes (chemical/mechanical clean during a planned outage) to restore clean heat transfer; E-201 is modelled as the heating side of evaporator unit V-201 in vrc_cal_v2_desup_hx
changes.rating_source: Data sheet Equipment ratings row: E-201 U 2,000 W/m2K in service, 2,500 W/m2K clean (marked ILLUSTRATIVE - confirm achieved clean coefficient by post-clean temperature/flow survey)

revisions.reason: Cheapest fix first: at 120% the fouled heater needs 9,794 m2 of 8,800 m2; restoring the documented clean coefficient of 2,500 W/m2K drops the need to 7,836 m2 (89%, run vrc_120_fixedturb_cleanK_E301steamcap). No new equipment and no rating is changed.

revisions.title: Add a small parallel vapour compressor K-202

changes.rating_source: vendor quote to confirm / standard size 55 t/h suction, 2,400 kW shaft at pressure ratio 1.8 (3.08 bar discharge) - proposed rating only, not an existing rating

revisions.reason: K-201 is a fixed-throughput machine (data sheet: vapour above its 226.8 t/h suction capacity is the excess vapour). At 120% it is short by about 49.5 t/h; a parallel 55 t/h machine leaves K-201 at its rating and runs itself at 90% flow / 85.5% power (run vrc_120_fixedturb_cleanK_E301steamcap). Existing ratings are untouched.

revisions.title: Hold purge-heater steam at today's rate by trimming the overhead split
revisions.reason: Operating change only: reducing the excess-vapour share to the purge heater from 8.44% to 7.03% of the overhead keeps its steam at 20,899 kg/h (today's rate) so its area need stays at 1,326 m2 of 1,500 m2 (88.4%) at 120% feed, instead of 106% with the share unchanged (runs vrc_120_fixedturb_nofix vs vrc_120_fixedturb_cleanK_E301steamcap). The extra vapour instead goes through the new parallel compressor. No rating is changed.

pssr: Plan and record the cleaning of E-201 (heating side of V-201); run a performance test after cleaning to confirm U of about 2,500 W/m²K.
Confirm the new branch tee in the field (model node K-201_SPLIT), including branch isolation valves, drains, vents and flow direction.
Isolation: confirm block valves on each nozzle of new K-202 before the line is opened to process fluid.
Check valves and backflow: confirm a non-return device so parallel K-202 cannot be driven backwards. To confirm.
Controls and parallel load sharing: confirm how K-202 shares load with the existing machine, including a manual fallback. To confirm.
Alarms and trips: confirm process and machine alarms and trips for new K-202 before start-up. To confirm.
Relief review: confirm relief protection for new K-202 and the changed piping. This file does not size a relief device.
Commissioning: confirm line-up, rotation and a no-load check of new K-202 before process fluid.
Materials and wet-service suitability of new K-202: to confirm. No materials certificate is on file.

Vendor curve for new K-202: to confirm against vendor quote to confirm / standard size 55 t/h suction, 2,400 kW shaft at pressure ratio 1.8 (3.08 bar discharge) - proposed rating only, not an existing rating. The rating in this file is provisional.
Turndown and surge: confirm the surge line, anti-surge control and minimum flow for new compressor K-202. To confirm; no vendor curve is on file.
Confirm the new join tee in the field (model node K201_JOIN), including branch isolation valves, drains, vents and flow direction.
Walk down the new tie-in at the inlet of K-201; confirm valves, drains, vents and flow direction match the Rev B drawing.
Set the new split at OVERHEAD_SPLIT branch: share of flow to this line 8.4 → 7.0 %; confirm the flow control can hold it at the new rate and update the operating procedure.
Update the P&ID, equipment datasheets and the operating procedure for every change above.
Brief the operators on the new setpoints before start-up.
Record the first 24 h of operation at the new throughput and compare with the model's predicted values in this file.

relief.detail: relief 7002/PSV-202 only through 3003/C1: if one is closed the side has no relief
relief.why: a heat-exchanger side that can be blocked in while the other side is hot: liquid thermal expansion can exceed the design pressure (API 521 hydraulic expansion; Williams Geismar 2013)
